## Overview

Full Hydrology and Water Resources section of an Environmental Impact Report (EIR), prepared over a 20-week course in Advanced Environmental Impact Analysis at UCSB. The project required a complete CEQA-style assessment of hydrologic impacts for a hypothetical faculty housing and classroom development adjacent to campus.

**Document scope:** 60+ pages covering environmental baseline, impact analysis, significance determination, and mitigation, all formatted to CEQA standards.

## Scope

This project is a full Environmental Impact Report (EIR) prepared over a 20-week course in Advanced Environmental Impact Analysis at UCSB. The assignment required a full assessment of hydrologic impacts associated with a hypothetical faculty housing and classroom development adjacent to campus under a CEQA framework.

My role focused on:

- conducting site visits to characterize existing watershed conditions;
- reviewing stormwater infrastructure and water quality data for the project area;
- evaluating short and long-term project impacts in the context of CEQA significance thresholds;
- developing mitigation measures and environmentally superior alternatives.

This project strengthened my technical understanding of stormwater regulations under the Clean Water Act while providing hands-on experience applying CEQA methodology to environmental compliance scenarios. 

## Hydrologic Setting

Baseline analysis included:

- Watershed boundaries, slopes, and drainage pathways
- Precipitation patterns and seasonal runoff characteristics

## Impact Analysis Under CEQA

Formal CEQA assessments examining:

- Runoff generation and peak flow changes from increased impervious surfaces
- Flood risk and stormwater pollution potential
- Alterations to local stream hydrology during storm events
- Pollutant loading and water quality degradation (metals, nutrients, sediments)
- Compliance with SWMPP, NPDES, and SWRCB regulations

## Mitigation Measures

Feasible CEQA mitigation strategies developed:

- Bioretention and infiltration basins
- Permeable pavement systems
- Construction-phase BMPs and SWPPP measures
- Environmentally superior project alternatives
